// upload(name, bytes, url) sends a file to the upload server. Files over 5 MB are refused before sending.
const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;

function checkSize(bytes) {
  if (bytes.length > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error(`file too large: ${bytes.length} bytes`);
}

async function upload(name, bytes, url = 'http://127.0.0.1:4599/upload') {
  checkSize(bytes);
  const res = await fetch(`${url}?name=${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, { method: 'POST', body: bytes });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`upload failed: ${res.status}`);
  return (await res.json()).id;
}

module.exports = { upload, checkSize, MAX_BYTES };

I changed `test/upload.test.js` so the upload test starts its own server. The suite now passes locally, 2 of 2.

The test used to call `upload()` against the hard-coded `127.0.0.1:4599`, and nothing listens there in CI. It now starts a small `node:http` server on a free port and returns `{id: 'abc123'}`. It passes that URL to `upload()`, which already accepts a `url` argument, so I didn't touch `upload.js`. The test still exercises the real `fetch` and JSON-parsing path, and it closes the server when it finishes.

This test doesn't check the real server's behavior. If you want that covered, it needs a separate integration job that starts the actual server.

I haven't run it in the CI environment itself. This folder has no `.github/workflows`, so I couldn't see how CI invokes the tests. I expect it to pass there, since it only needs loopback networking.
